title: New balance keys parse via truncating jint — a decimal value silently passes the 'fail-fast' > 0 check
evidence: core/catalog.odin:487: `b.lane_queue_packets = jint(obj, "lane_queue_packets", 0)`; :491: `b.pool_max_packets = jint(obj, "pool_max_packets", 0)`; jint body (:676-683): `#partial switch x in v { case json.Integer: return i32(x); case json.Float:   return i32(x) }` — a json.Float is coerced with i32(x), so `"lane_queue_packets": 1.5` parses to 1 and passes the `<= 0` rejection; the codebase's strict accessor exists for exactly this case (:690-694): `jint_strict :: proc(o: json.Object, key: string, def: i32) -> (i32, bool) { if v, ok := o[key]; ok { #partial switch x in v { case json.Integer: return i32(x), true; case json.Float:   return 0, false } } ... }` and lane_presets weights reject non-integers (catalog.odin: `wv, okv := warr[wi].(json.Integer); if !okv { return {"balance.json", lp.id, "weights must be integers"} }`).
detail: The diff claims the two 3.3 keys are 'fail-fast validated' — a decimal ≥ 1 silently truncates to a valid bound instead of aborting load, violating ODN-5 fail-fast + the integer-only bar (ODN-10) that the sibling validations enforce.
recommended_fix: Parse the two new keys with jint_strict (reject json.Float) or a json.Integer type-assert like the lane_presets weights loop; add a decimal fail-fast test row.
